passage: Our neighborhood association wants to put two compost bins behind the rec center. So now we're supposed to sort every scrap of food we eat and turn our kitchens into science labs? Some of us have jobs. Hard pass.
cue: sort every scrap of food we eat and turn our kitchens into science labs
explanation: The proposal is two optional bins behind the rec center. Kelsey argues against a far more extreme plan, mandatory sorting of every scrap at home, that nobody suggested.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: Kelsey stays on the compost topic; she exaggerates what the proposal asks for instead of changing the subject.

passage:
Aisha: Could we pause new features for one sprint and fix the top ten crash bugs?
Tom: So Aisha thinks we should stop building the product entirely and just polish what we have forever. Customers pay for features, not for polish.
cue: stop building the product entirely and just polish what we have forever
explanation: Aisha asked for one sprint focused on crash bugs. Tom turns that into a permanent halt on all new work, then argues against that instead.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: Tom isn't claiming there are only two choices; he's misdescribing the single, limited thing Aisha proposed.

title: Re: Friday practice times
passage: Thanks for writing, Mrs. Tran. I hear that some parents would like Friday practice to end at 6 instead of 7 so the kids can finish homework, and I get it. But if we treat practice as something kids can skip whenever homework comes up, we're telling them commitment doesn't matter.
cue: treat practice as something kids can skip whenever homework comes up
explanation: The parents asked to end Friday practice an hour earlier. Coach Delaney answers a different request, letting kids skip whenever they like, and rejects that one.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: He responds on the topic of practice times, but to a distorted version of the request rather than an unrelated issue.

title: Sugar Plan Sparks Fight Over Class Parties
passage: Dietitians advising the Pinecrest school board recommended Tuesday that added sugar in cafeteria lunches be cut by 20 percent over three years. Opponents told the board the plan amounts to a ban on birthday treats in every classroom.
cue: the plan amounts to a ban on birthday treats in every classroom
explanation: The recommendation covers cafeteria lunches and a gradual 20 percent cut. The opponents argue against a classroom ban on birthday treats, which isn't part of the plan.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: No either-or choice is being forced; the opponents are distorting what the dietitians actually recommended.

source: Mayor Colleen Hart · Budget town hall
passage: My colleague on the council has argued that we should review the parks budget line by line before approving it. I respect the instinct to be careful with your money. But I won't support a view that says our parks are a waste of money and that families don't deserve green space.
cue: a view that says our parks are a waste of money
explanation: The council member asked for a line-by-line review. Mayor Hart recasts that as believing parks are a waste of money, a position the council member never took.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: The mayor stays on the parks budget; the problem is that she swaps the actual request for a harsher one.

title: The critics missed the point
passage: I've used the Lumen 4 e-reader for two months. Some reviewers complained that the screen is dim in direct sunlight, which is true at the lowest setting. Their argument boils down to "no one should ever read outdoors with this," and that's just silly. Bump the brightness and it's fine.
cue: no one should ever read outdoors with this
explanation: The reviewers said the screen is dim in direct sun. Ellis inflates that into a claim that nobody should read outdoors at all, which is much easier to call silly.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: Ellis isn't limiting the options to two; he's rewording the critics' complaint into something more extreme.

passage:
Wren: I think we should ask the landlord to fix the laundry room before we push on parking.
Sam: Just so I've got it right: laundry first, parking later, not parking never? Then I agree. Half the machines have been broken since June.
cue: laundry first, parking later, not parking never?
explanation: Sam checks that he's describing Wren's view fairly before responding, then agrees for a concrete reason. Nothing gets distorted.

whyNot.fal_straw_man: Sam restates Wren's position accurately and asks her to confirm it. A straw man would exaggerate it instead.

source: Trustee Mei Lin · Riverside library board
passage: The proposal in front of us, in its own words, closes the Westside branch on weekends to save $85,000. I won't pretend it does more than that. But weekends bring 40 percent of Westside's visits, according to the proposal's own appendix, so those savings come at a real cost.
cue: in its own words, closes the Westside branch on weekends to save $85,000
explanation: Trustee Lin quotes the proposal directly, refuses to exaggerate it, and then uses its own figures to argue the cost is high. That's a fair critique.

whyNot.fal_straw_man: She states the plan exactly as written and argues against what it really does, using the proposal's own appendix.
